key_insight: Retention-constrained fine-tuning improves aluminium MACE defect predictions while preserving the tested near-equilibrium mechanical and vibrational response.
engineering_relevance: The protocol supports more reliable atomistic simulations of defect dynamics and plasticity without sacrificing validated bulk behaviour.
method: Acquire configurations using conditional force uncertainty from sensitivities over 144 readout weights.
Iteratively update all model parameters with relative-energy anchoring to retain historical behaviour.
Gate updates against historical elastic-group energy and vibrational tolerances.
evidence_signal: With 32 acquired configurations and 400 gradient updates, force-uncertainty selection reduced mean development force error from 22.43 to 21.52 meV/Å, outperforming three sampling baselines; all three runs met retention criteria with phonon RMS drift below 0.05 THz.
watch_item: Retention is demonstrated only for the tested aluminium configurations and tolerances; deployment requires compatible reference energies and acceptance checks.
paper_title: Retention-constrained fine-tuning of a pre-trained aluminium MACE potential for non-equilibrium defect dynamics and plasticity
